title: Edmonton's Hot Streak Wins Games, Though the Chances Say Cool Off
dek: The Oilers went 3-0 on a shooting run the numbers say can't last, while Vancouver sank to 2-9-1 and New Jersey bought Hellebuyck.
text:
The best team in the league this week might also be the luckiest, and the evidence is hard to ignore. Edmonton went 3-0, outscored opponents 16-10 and sits second overall at 8-1-1. The chances tell a quieter story: the Oilers got exactly 50 percent of the expected goals (a measure of the quality of shots each side generated). They won on finishing, not on dominance.

## The Oilers' Finishing Run

Connor McDavid has points in 10 straight games (8 goals, 23 assists) and had 13 points this week alone. Leon Draisaitl added nine points, with five goals. Evan Bouchard has points in seven straight.

The numbers behind them are the catch. McDavid has 8 goals on 4.4 expected, shooting 32 percent against 16 percent last season. Draisaitl has 10 goals on 5.6 expected, shooting 28 percent against 19. Bouchard has 7 goals on 1.7 expected, shooting 23 percent against 10. The chances are real, but that finishing rate rarely lasts. Ten games is a small sample, and Edmonton's results will probably drift toward its chances.

Thursday's game showed both sides of it. Edmonton beat Carolina 6-5 in a shootout, with Draisaitl the star. Expected goals were nearly even, 2.94 for Carolina and 2.86 for Edmonton, and Edmonton deserved to win 48 percent of the time (the share of simulated replays of every shot that the team wins). Carolina still leads the league at 8-2-2 for 18 points, and Mark Jankowski has scored in six straight games, six goals in all.

## Robbery in Washington, a Rout That Wasn't

The week's biggest steal came on Tuesday. Los Angeles beat Washington 5-2 despite 3.14 expected goals to Washington's 4.68, and the Kings deserved to win just 21 percent of the time. Artemi Panarin was the star. On Sunday, Minnesota beat Columbus only 2-1 while generating 5.18 expected goals to 1.37, a game the Wild deserved to win 90 percent of the time. Kirill Kaprizov was the star there. One goal was all Columbus's goaltending would give up.

## Goalies and Goals

Yaroslav Askarov of San Jose owned the week in net: 74 shots, four goals against, a .946 save percentage and 5.2 goals saved above expected. That means he stopped about five more goals than an average goalie would have on the same shots. Karel Vejmelka of Utah had the opposite week, a .769 save percentage on 39 shots, nine goals allowed and 4.9 goals worse than expected.

Mikko Rantanen scored a hat trick for Dallas on Tuesday, and Florida's Sam Bennett and Carter Verhaeghe each scored three in the same game on Saturday. The least likely goal of the week belonged to Montreal's Kaiden Guhle, a wrist shot against Chicago given a 0.6 percent chance. Tampa Bay's Victor Hedman and New Jersey's Arseny Gritsyuk had 0.9 percent shots of their own.

Some players are due for better luck. Pavel Dorofeyev of the Rangers has 2 goals on 5.7 expected and led the week in chances without a goal (2.3 expected). Minnesota's Joel Eriksson Ek has 2 on 7.1.

## Up and Down

Dallas had the best week, going 3-0 with 60 percent of the expected goals and four straight wins in all. That one looks real. Boston has points in seven straight, and Detroit has points in six. Philadelphia also went 3-0.

At the bottom, Vancouver is 2-9-1, winless in nine (0-8-1) and outscored 41-18, with 35 percent of the expected goals. Anaheim is winless in five and was outscored 20-9 in that run. Chicago, 3-7-0, scored one goal and allowed eight in two games.

## Hellebuyck Heads to Jersey

Friday brought the week's big move. New Jersey acquired goalie Connor Hellebuyck from Winnipeg for forwards Dawson Mercer, Alexander Command and Nick Bjugstad, goalie Nicolas Daws, a 2029 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick. The fit is clear: the Devils are 6-4-0 and control 58.6 percent of the expected goals, yet their goaltending has been 5.3 goals worse than expected. Winnipeg, meanwhile, is winless in four (0-2-2).

## Milestones

Ian Cole played his 1,000th game for Chicago. Nikolaj Ehlers reached 600 career points, Alex DeBrincat 300 goals, and Auston Matthews, Jack Eichel, Brandon Carlo and Frank Vatrano each played their 700th game.
